title: Decide: foxtrot fast-forward defeats the date clamp
description: From core-dates (26f41f4). A contributor merges main into their own backdated branch (their branch becomes first parent); a maintainer fast-forwards to it. The contributor's commits then form HEAD's first-parent line, so query --at counts their record from its forged date; no date clamp can catch it. Options: (a) process only: --no-ff, documented as the only defence (implemented in DESIGN, eeaf899); (b) check warns when a first-parent merge is dated before its second parent (also fires on honest merges after clock skew). Agent recommendation: (a). Also confirm: a side-branch commit takes the effective date of the first first-parent commit that contains it (implemented).
close_reason: Decision (Mark 2026-10-24): process only. Registry merges are --no-ff (DESIGN, docs/bridge-deployment.md); no code.
